newsitem.title: FRANCE: WorldSpace sees investment rise to $1 bln by 1999.
newsitem.headline: WorldSpace sees investment rise to $1 bln by 1999.

text.p: WorldSpace Inc, a private company setting up a satellite-based digital audio broadcasting (DAB) service for developing countries, said it expected to increase annual investment to $1 billion by 1999.
"Our investment, currently $750 million, should reach one billion dollars by 1999," chairman Noah Samara, in Toulouse to lay the cornerstone of a technical centre, told Reuters.

"Our network will consist of three satellites, AfriStar, AsiaStar et CaribStar, which will be launched respectively on June 16, 1998, December 16, 1998, and June 16, 1999, to cover Africa and the Middle East, Asia and Latin America," he said.
"Once the satellites are launched, WorldSpace will probably seek a share listing in New York or London," he said. "But we have time to think about it. For the time being, we don't need capital."
WorldSpace is privately owned and Samara declined to detail the ownership structure.

"From 1998, electronics retailers will be able to furnish receivers for the WorldSpace service for around $100. In the future, our objective is to have this as an option, in the form a chip, which would not greatly increase the price of a TV," he said in an interview.

Samara said he hoped WorldSpace would start to show a profit in around four years based on sales of three to four million receivers in its first two years of operations and 10 to 15 million in each of the next two years. Sales should rise to between 15 to 20 million after six or seven years, he said.
He said the areas covered by its satellites comprised markets with TV sales totalling around 100 million a year.
"Today, we don't have any real competitors. In any case, our technical lead is considerable," Samara said.
WorldSpace expected to create 500 jobs immediately, including 50 in France through a subsidiary to be established in Toulouse, probably in the next month, Samara said.
WorldSpace signed a chip development deal with SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV in June and its industrial partners in France include Alcatel Alsthom, Matra-Marconi and Arianespace.
